                  <ns0:head>CHAP. VI.</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p>IN the year that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Kings 15. 7.</ns0:note> king Uzziah died, I <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">John 12. 41.</ns0:note> saw <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">In a Vision or Ecstasie.</ns0:note> also the Lord <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Either, 1. God the Son, who frequently appeared to the Patriarchs and Prophets, and that sometimes in the form of a Man: Or rather, 2. the Divine Majesty as he subsisteth in Three Persons, as may be gathered both from the Plural Number <ns0:hi>
                           <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>s,</ns0:hi> used of this Lord, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 8. and by comparing other Scriptures; for God the Father is described as sitting upon a Throne, <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 7. 9, 13. and elsewhere; and the Glory of God here manifested<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> is said to be Christ's Glory, <ns0:hi>Iob.</ns0:hi> 12. 41. and the Words of the Lord here following, are said to be spoken by the Holy Ghost, <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 28. 25.</ns0:note> sitting upon a throne <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">In the posture of a Judge, to hear Causes, and give Sentence.</ns0:note>, high and lifted up <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Towards the Roof of the Temple.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> the skirts thereof.</ns0:note> his train <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Or, as the Word properly signifies, and is here rendred by divers, <ns0:hi>the skirts</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>borders of him,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>of it,</ns0:hi> to wit, his Royal and Judicial Robe; for he is represented as a Judge.</ns0:note> filled the tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">His glorious Robes reached down to the bottom of the Temple, and were spread abroad in the Temple, which was an Evidence of a more than ordinary Majesty. <ns0:hi>The Temple</ns0:hi> may be here taken either, 1. largely, and so it includes the Courts as well as the House, as that Word is oft used; or, 2. strictly, for the House it self, or for that part of the Temple in which this Vision was exhibited, which may seem to have been the Porch, for that was much higher than the other Parts.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2 Above it stood <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">As Ministers attending upon their Lord, and waiting to receive and execute his Commands.</ns0:note> the Seraphims <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Certain holy and blessed Angels, thus called from <ns0:hi>fire</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>burning,</ns0:hi> which this Word properly signifies; to represent either, 1. their Nature, which is bright and glorious, subtil, and pure, and spiritual, like Fire; or, 2. their Property, of fervent Zeal for God's Service and Glory; or, 3<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> their Office and pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sent Employment, which was to execute God's Vengeance upon the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> and to burn them up like Dross.</ns0:note>: each one had six wings; <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ezek. 1. 11.</ns0:note> with twain he covered his face <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Out of profound Reverence, as being so sensible of the infinite di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stance between God and him<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> that he durst not presume to look directly upon him, and judg'd himself neither able nor worthy to behold the Brightness of his Glory.</ns0:note>, and with twain he covered his feet <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, 1. his secret Parts, which sometimes come under that name, as <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 28. 57. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 7. 20. & 36. 12. of which see more in my <ns0:hi>Latin Synopsis</ns0:hi> upon <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 4. 25. And so this is done for our <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>nstruction, to teach us Modesty and Chastity: Or, 2. their Feet properly so called, as that Word is gene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rally used; from which use we should not depart without necessity, which, with submission, seems not to be in this place. And so this may signifie a sence of their own natu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ral, though not moral Infirmity, and a desire that God would not too severely examine all their Ways and Actions, which <ns0:hi>the feet</ns0:hi> commonly signifie, because though they did not swerve from God's Commands, yet they were not worthy of the acceptation, nor suitable to the Dignity of so glorious a Majesty.</ns0:note>, and with twain he did flie <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Which signifies their great for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wardness and expedition in executing God's Commands. Comp. <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 9. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>1.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3 And <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> this cried to this.</ns0:note> one cried unto another <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Singing in Consort the Praises of their Lord.</ns0:note>, and said, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rev. 4. 3.</ns0:note> Holy, holy, holy <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> is repeated thrice, either, 1. to intimate the Trinity of Persons united in the Divine Essence<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> or, 2. that he was most eminently and unquestionably holy in his present Work of Judgment, and in all his Ways; such Repetitions being very frequent in Scripture, for the greater assurance of the thing, as <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 7. 4. <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 21. 9.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the LORD of hosts, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> his glo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry is the ful<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness of the whole earth.</ns0:note> the whole earth <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Not onely <ns0:hi>Conaan,</ns0:hi> to which the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> did vainly and arrogantly confine the Pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sence of God, but all the World<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Which seems to have a respect to the Conversion of the Gentiles, which did accom<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pany the plenary and last Execution of this Judgment here threatned against the Jewish Nation, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 10. as is evident by comparing this with <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 13. 14, 15. <ns0:hi>& Act.</ns0:hi> 28. 19. and other places of the New Testament.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> full of his glory <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Of the Effects and Demonstrations of his glorious Holiness, as well as of his Power, and Wisdom, and Goodness.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:568" />4 And the posts of the <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> thre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> door <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Together with the Door it self, as if the Door was to be removed, and the Temple thereby to be exposed to the view and rapine of profane Persons. Such violent Motions were commonly Tokens of God's Anger.</ns0:note> moved at the voice of him that cried <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">To wit, the Angel, which cried, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 3.</ns0:note>, and the house was filled with smoak <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Which elsewhere is a Token of God's Presence and Acceptance, as <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 40. 34. 1 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 8. 10. but here of his Anger, as <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 18. 8. and elsewhere.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 Then said I, Wo <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> me, for I am <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> cut off.</ns0:note> undone, because I <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi> a man of unclean lips <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">I am a great Sinner, as many other ways, so particular<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly by my Lips, which being in a special manner consecrated to God by my Prophetical Office, should have been intirely devoted to him: But, alas! my Speeches, either to God in Prayer, or from God in Preaching and Prophecying to the People, have been mixed and defiled with so much irreve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rence, dulness, distraction of Thoughts and Affections, car<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nal Fear, and many other Infirmities, that I dread the thoughts of appearing before thy Judgment-seat, which I see erected in this place. For <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> had been a Prophet be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore this time, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 1. 1. and was now called, not in general to his Prophetical Office, but to the delivery of this special Message.</ns0:note>, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">I am an unclean Branch of an unclean Tree, and, besides my own Uncleanness, I have both by my Omissi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons and Commissions involved my self in the guilt of their Sins, and therefore may justly fear to partake with them in their Plagues.</ns0:note>: for mine eyes have seen the king, the LORD of hosts <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">The sight of this glorious and holy God gives me cause to fear that he is come to Judgment against me, together with others. Whilst Sinners are secure and presumptuous, the holiest Persons have ever been filled with great Reverence, and oft times with Doubts and Fears, at any extraordinary Manifestation of God's Presence. See <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 16<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 13. & 17. 3. <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 13. 23.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 Then flew one of the Seraphims unto me <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">By Gods Command.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> and in his hand a live coal.</ns0:note> having a live coal <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Both a Token and an Instru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment of Purification, as the next Verse explains it.</ns0:note> in his hand, <ns0:hi>which</ns0:hi> he had taken with the tongs from off the altar <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Of Burnt-offering, which stood in the Court of the Priests near the Porch, and which had always Coals of Fire upon it, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 6. 12, 13. Hence he took it, to shew that Men are to expect Purification and Expiation of Sin onely by such means as God hath appointed, and particularly by Christ, whom that Altar did manifestly represent, <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 13. 10.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 And he <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> caused it to touch.</ns0:note> laid <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> upon my mouth <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Sleightly, so as onely to touch my Lips, and not to burn them; which God could easily effect.</ns0:note>, and said, Lo, this hath touched thy lips, and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> attoned, or, expiated.</ns0:note> purged <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">This is a Sign that I have pardoned and purged the Uncleanness of thy Lips, and do own and accept thee as a fit Minister for my Ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vice.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 Also I heard the voice of the Lord, say<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, Whom shall I send, and who will go for <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 1. 26.</ns0:note> us <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">To deliver the following Message. The change of the Number, <ns0:hi>I</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>us,</ns0:hi> is very remarkable; and both <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ing meant of one and the same Lord, do sufficiently intimate a Plurality of Persons in the Godhead.</ns0:note>? Then said I, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> behold me.</ns0:note> Here <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi> I, send me <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">God's last and great Favour to him did both encourage and oblige him to be forward in God's Service.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 And he said, Go and tell this people <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Not <ns0:hi>my people,</ns0:hi> for I disown them, as they have rejected me.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 13. 14. Mar. 4. 12. Luk. 8. 10. Joh. 12. 40. Act. 28. 26. Rom. 11. 8.</ns0:note> Hear ye <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> without ceasing, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> Hear ye in hear<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> indeed, but understand not; and <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> in see<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing.</ns0:note> see ye indeed, but perceive not <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> Words are Imperative; yet they are not to be taken as a Command what the People ought to do, but onely as a Signification and Prediction what by their own Wickedness, and by God's just Judgment, they did and would do, as is manifest by <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 13. 14. <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 28. 26. where they are so rendred. And Imperative<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Words among the <ns0:hi>Hebrews</ns0:hi> are frequently put for the future, as is well known to the Learned. The sence is, Because you have so long heard my Words, and seen my Works, to no purpose, and have hardned your Hearts, and will not learn <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>or re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />form, I will punish you in your own kind, your Sin shall be your Punishment. I will still continue my Word and Works to you, not in Mercy, and for your Good, but to aggravate your Sin and Condemnation; for I will blind your Minds, and withdraw my Spirit, so that you shall be as un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />able, as now you are unwilling, to understand or perceive any thing that may do you good.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 Make the heart of this people fat <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Stupid and senseless: For the Fat which is in the Body is without sense; and Fatness in the Heart, makes it dull and heavy. Thus this Phrase is used, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 119. 70. And this seems best to agree with the following Words. This making of their Hearts fat is here ascribed to the Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phet, as it is ascribed to God in the repetition of this Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phecy, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 12. 40. because God inflicted this Judgment up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on them by the Ministry of the Prophet, partly by way of Prediction, foretelling that this would be the effect of his Preaching; and partly by way of Judicial Operation, withdrawing the Light and Help of his Spirit, and giving them up to the Power and Arts of Satan, and to their own Mistakes and Lusts, whereby they are easily and commonly led to turn God's Word, as they do other things, into Occa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sions of Sin.</ns0:note>, and make their ears heavy <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Make them dull of hearing, as <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 59 1. <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 7. 11. as sometimes the Ears are made by an exces<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sive Noise.</ns0:note>, and shut their eyes <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>dawb their eyes,</ns0:hi> as the Word is used also <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 44. 18.</ns0:note>: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Jer. 5. 21.</ns0:note> lest they see <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">That they may not be able, as before they were not willing, to see.</ns0:note> with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Turn from their sinful Practi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces, unto God.</ns0:note> and be healed <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Of Sin, which is the Disease of the Soul, by Remission and Sanctification, and of all the deadly Ef<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fects of Sin.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 Then said I, Lord how long <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">An abrupt Speech, arising from the Prophets great Passion and Astonishment: How long shall this dreadful Judgment last?</ns0:note>? And he an<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swered, Until the cities be wasted without inhabi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tant, and the houses without man, and the land be <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> desolate with desola<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion.</ns0:note> utterly desolate <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Until this land be totally destroyed, first by the <ns0:hi>Babylonians,</ns0:hi> and afterward by the <ns0:hi>Romans.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12 And the LORD have removed men far a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />way <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Hath caused this People to be carried away Captive into far Countries.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:hi>there</ns0:hi> be a great forsaking in the midst of the land <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Till Houses and Lands be generally forsaken of their Owners, either because fled away from the Sword into strange Lands, or because they went into Captivity.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 But yet in it <ns0:hi>shall be</ns0:hi> a tenth <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">A small Remnant reserved, that Number being put in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />definitely, as is very usual.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> when it is returned, and hath been broused.</ns0:note> and <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> shall return <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">To wit, out of the <ns0:hi>Babylonish</ns0:hi> Captivity, into their own Land.</ns0:note>, and shall be eaten <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">That Remnant shall be devoured and destroyed a second time, by the Kings of <ns0:hi>Syria,</ns0:hi> and afterwards more effectually by the <ns0:hi>Romans.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>: as a teil-tree, and as an oak <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Or, Yet <ns0:hi>as,</ns0:hi> &c. Or, Nevertheless <ns0:hi>a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>
                        </ns0:hi> &c. such Particles being frequently understood in the <ns0:hi>Hebrew,</ns0:hi> as hath been noted again and again. So the Sence of the following Words of the Verse seems to be this, Although the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Nation shall undergo a second and a greater Desolation by the <ns0:hi>Romans,</ns0:hi> yet there shall be another Remnant, not such an one as that which came out of <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> which, for the most part, were corrupt and degenerate, as appears by the Sacred Histories and Prophesies relating to that time; but an Holy Seed, a number of Elect and Godly <ns0:hi>Israelites,</ns0:hi> who shall afterwards look upon him whom they pierced, and mourn over him, as is said <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 12. 10. and by me be received to Mercy.</ns0:note> whose <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> stock and sten<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> substance <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> in them, when they cast <ns0:hi>their leaves</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Who when their Leaves are withered and cast, as it is in Winter, have a Substance, or Subsistence, or Support within themselves, to wit, a Vital Principle, which preserves Life in the Root and Body of the Tree, and in due time sends it forth into all the Branches. But others take the <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> Word, <ns0:hi>Shallecheth,</ns0:hi> for the Proper name of a Place, to wit, a Causeway which led from the Palace to the Temple, 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 26. 16. and so the Place is and may be rendred thus, <ns0:hi>As a teil-tree</ns0:hi> (or, <ns0:hi>
                           <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>n elm) and as an oak</ns0:hi> (the Singu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lar Number for the Plural, as is very frequent) <ns0:hi>As the elms and the oaks which</ns0:hi> are <ns0:hi>at</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>by Shallecheth</ns0:hi> (on both sides of which Way such Trees were planted, to beautifie and to support that Causeway, as some have observed) <ns0:hi>have <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                              <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>
                        </ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>support in them,</ns0:hi> either, 1. for themselves; they stand fast and firm, when other Trees are blown down: or, for the Way which they uphold.</ns0:note>: so the holy seed <ns0:hi>shall be</ns0:hi> the substance thereof <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Or rather, <ns0:hi>the support</ns0:hi> (as the same Word seems to be taken in the next foregoing Clause) <ns0:hi>thereof,</ns0:hi> to wit, of the Land or People, which, were it not for the sake of these Elect Persons, should be totally and finally rooted out; or, of that Tenth part, which shall be delivered and preserved for the sake of that Holy Seed, those true-hearted <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> which are among them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
